column3: NASB follows the critical text; it adds “that was there” and renders “the Cyrenian” as “of Cyrene.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “sent them off” as “sent them away.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “were proclaiming” as “began to proclaim.”
NASB follows the critical text; it moves “Jewish” before “false prophet.”
NASB renders “an intelligent man” as “a man of intelligence” and “desired” as “sought.”
NASB puts the explanation of the name in parentheses.
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “known as.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “craft” as “fraud” and “perverting” as “make crooked.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “one to lead” as “those who would lead.”
NASB renders “astonished” as “amazed.”
NASB follows the critical text; “those around Paul” is rendered “Paul and his companions.”
NASB follows the critical text with “Pisidian Antioch.”
NASB follows the critical text; “rulers of the synagogue” is rendered “synagogue officials.”
NASB renders “made a sign” as “motioning.”
NASB follows the critical text; “exalted” is rendered “made … great,” and “sojourn” is “stay.”
NASB renders “endured their ways” as “put up with them”; some manuscripts read “cared for them.”
NASB follows the critical text; it moves “about four hundred and fifty years,” which opens v. 20 in the Greek, into this verse, adding “all of which took.”
NASB begins after the phrase moved to v. 19; it adds “them.”
NASB adds “for.”
NASB adds “to be” and “concerning whom”; part of the quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“has brought”); “seed” is rendered “offspring.”
NASB renders “before the face of His coming” as “before His coming.”
NASB follows the critical text (“What”); it renders the imperfect as “kept saying.”
NASB follows the critical text (“to us”); “brothers” is rendered “Brethren.”
NASB renders “voices” as “utterances” and restructures the verse.
NASB adds “though” and “ground for putting Him to death.”
NASB follows the critical text; “tree” is rendered “cross.”
Close to the Greek.
